- Model consistently overestimates early in the 30-day horizon, especially after sharp price spikes; reduce forecast by 1–2% for the first 5–7 days.
- Model tends to overshoot peak prices in the final 5–7 days of the forecast; cap forecast at 1–2% below the 30-day moving average of true values.
- Forecast shows persistent lag in capturing true price reversals; adjust for mean reversion by adding 0.5–1.0% of the 30-day average deviation to the forecast if the model is below true values for 3 consecutive days.
- When true values show a strong upward trend, model underestimates the magnitude; increase forecast by 1–3% for the last 5 days if the true trend is >1.5% per day.
- Model often fails to account for seasonal or event-driven volatility; apply a 0.5–1.5% upward adjustment if the true value exceeds the 30-day moving average by >1.5% for 2+ consecutive days.
